verses.text: Yahweh called Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting.
“Tell the Israelites this: ‘Whenever one of you brings an offering to Yahweh, bring it from your cattle, sheep, or goats.
“‘Bringing a burnt offering from your cattle? Pick a male with no defects. Bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting so Yahweh will accept you.
Put your hand on the animal’s head. It’ll be accepted on your behalf to make atonement for you.
Slaughter the bull there before Yahweh. Aaron’s sons, the priests, will bring the blood and splash it against all sides of the altar at the tent’s entrance.
Skin the animal and cut it into pieces.
Aaron’s sons will light a fire on the altar and stack the wood over the flames. 🔥
Then they’ll lay out the pieces, including the head and the fat, on the wood over the altar fire.
Rinse the insides and legs with water. The priest will burn the whole thing on the altar. It’s a burnt offering, given through fire, and its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
“‘Bringing a sheep or goat as a burnt offering? Pick a male with no defects.
Slaughter it before Yahweh on the north side of the altar. Aaron’s sons, the priests, will splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
Cut it into pieces. The priest will lay the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood over the altar fire.
Rinse the insides and legs with water. The priest will offer the whole thing and burn it on the altar. It’s a burnt offering, given through fire, and its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
“‘Giving a bird to Yahweh as a burnt offering? Bring a turtledove or a young pigeon.
The priest will take it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn the head there. He’ll drain the bird’s blood down the side of the altar.
He’ll remove the bird’s food pouch and feathers and toss them where the ashes go, east of the altar.
He’ll tear the bird open by its wings, keeping it in one piece. Then he’ll burn it on the wood over the altar fire. It’s a burnt offering, given through fire, and its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.’”
“‘Bringing Yahweh a grain offering? Use fine flour, pour oil over it, and add frankincense.

Take it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest will take a handful of the fine flour and oil, along with all the frankincense, and burn that portion on the altar as a reminder. It’s an offering given through fire, and its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
The rest of the grain offering goes to Aaron and his sons. It’s a most holy part of the offerings given to Yahweh through fire.
“‘Baking your grain offering in the oven? Make cakes with fine flour mixed with oil or thin wafers brushed with oil. Leave out the yeast either way.
Making it on a griddle? Mix fine flour with oil and leave out the yeast.
Break it into pieces and pour oil over it. That’s your grain offering.
Making your grain offering in a pan? Use fine flour and oil.
Bring the grain offering you’ve prepared to Yahweh. Hand it to the priest, and he’ll take it to the altar.
The priest will take out the portion that serves as a reminder and burn it on the altar. It’s an offering given through fire, and its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
The rest goes to Aaron and his sons. It’s a most holy part of the offerings given to Yahweh through fire.
“‘Keep yeast out of every grain offering you bring to Yahweh. Don’t burn any yeast or honey as an offering to him.
You can bring those to Yahweh as a first-harvest offering. They don’t go on the altar to make a pleasing smell.
Salt every grain offering. That salt belongs with your God’s covenant, so don’t leave it out. Bring salt with every offering. 🧂
“‘When you bring Yahweh a grain offering from your first harvest, take fresh heads of grain, roast them over the fire, and crush them.
Pour oil over the grain and put frankincense on it. That’s a grain offering.
The priest will burn some of the crushed grain and oil, plus all the frankincense, as the portion that serves as a reminder. It’s an offering given to Yahweh through fire.’”
“‘Bringing cattle as a peace offering? You can bring a male or a female before Yahweh. Either way, it must have no defects.
Put your hand on the animal’s head and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons, the priests, will splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
Give part of that peace offering to Yahweh through fire. Take the fat that covers the insides and all the fat attached to them.
Remove both kidneys, the fat on them near the lower back, and the piece that covers the liver. Take that piece out with the kidneys.
Aaron’s sons will burn those parts on top of the burnt offering, over the wood in the altar fire. It’s an offering given through fire, and its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
“‘Bringing a peace offering to Yahweh from your flock? Male or female, the animal must have no defects.
If you’re bringing a lamb, present it before Yahweh.
Put your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons will splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
Give the fat from that peace offering to Yahweh through fire. Cut away all the tail fat close to the backbone, and take the fat that covers the insides and all the fat attached to them.
Remove both kidneys, the fat on them near the lower back, and the piece that covers the liver. Take that piece out with the kidneys.
The priest will burn those parts on the altar as food offered to Yahweh through fire.
“‘If you’re bringing a goat, present it before Yahweh.
Put your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons will splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
Give these parts to Yahweh through fire. Take the fat that covers the insides and all the fat attached to them.
Remove both kidneys, the fat on them near the lower back, and the piece that covers the liver. Take that piece out with the kidneys.
The priest will burn those parts on the altar as food given through fire, with a pleasing smell. All the fat belongs to Yahweh.
“‘Here’s a rule to keep for every generation, wherever you live: Don’t eat fat or blood.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites this: ‘Suppose someone breaks one of Yahweh’s commands without meaning to and does something he said to stay away from.
If it’s the anointed priest who sins and brings guilt on the people, he must bring Yahweh a young bull with no defects as a sin offering for what he did.
Bring the bull before Yahweh at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Put a hand on its head and slaughter it there before Yahweh.
The anointed priest will take some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting.
He’ll dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before Yahweh, in front of the sanctuary curtain.

He’ll put some blood on the horns of the altar for fragrant incense, there before Yahweh inside the tent. Then he’ll pour the rest at the base of the altar for burnt offerings, at the tent’s entrance.
He’ll take all the fat from the bull brought as the sin offering, including the fat covering its insides and all the fat attached to them.
He’ll also remove both kidneys, the fat on them near the lower back, and the piece that covers the liver. That piece comes out with the kidneys.
Take those parts out the same way you would for a bull brought as a peace offering. The priest will burn them on the altar for burnt offerings. 🔥
He’ll take the bull’s hide, all its meat, its head, its legs, its insides, and its dung,
everything that’s left of the bull, out of the camp to the clean place where the ashes are dumped. He’ll burn it there over a wood fire, right at the ash dump.
“‘Suppose the whole community of Israel does something Yahweh told them to stay away from. They’re guilty, even though nobody in the assembly realizes what happened.
Once the community finds out what they did, they must bring a young bull in front of the Tent of Meeting as a sin offering.
The community’s elders will place their hands on the bull’s head before Yahweh, and the bull will be slaughtered there before him.
The anointed priest will take some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting.
He’ll dip his finger in it and sprinkle it seven times before Yahweh, in front of the curtain.
He’ll put some blood on the horns of the altar that stands before Yahweh inside the tent. He’ll pour the rest at the base of the altar for burnt offerings, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
He’ll remove all the bull’s fat and burn it on the altar.
Treat this bull the same way as the first bull brought as a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for the people, and they’ll be forgiven.
He’ll carry the bull out of the camp and burn it the way he burned the first one. That’s the assembly’s sin offering.
“‘Now suppose a ruler sins. Without realizing it, he does something Yahweh his God told him to stay away from, and he’s guilty.
When he finds out what he did, he must bring a male goat with no defects as his offering.
He’ll put his hand on its head and slaughter it before Yahweh at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered. That’s a sin offering.
The priest will use his finger to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He’ll pour the rest at the base of that altar.
He’ll burn all the fat on the altar, just like the fat from a peace offering. The priest will make atonement for what the ruler did, and the ruler will be forgiven.
“‘Suppose someone else in the community sins by accident. They do something Yahweh told them to stay away from, and they’re guilty.
When they find out what they did, they must bring a female goat with no defects as their offering for that sin.
They’ll put a hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it at the place set aside for burnt offerings.
The priest will use his finger to put some blood on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He’ll pour the rest at the base of the altar.

He’ll take out all the fat the way it’s taken out of a peace offering and burn it on the altar. Its smell will be pleasing to Yahweh. The priest will make atonement for that person, and they’ll be forgiven.
“‘If they bring a lamb as their sin offering, it must be a female with no defects.
They’ll put a hand on its head and slaughter it as a sin offering in the same place where burnt offerings are slaughtered.
The priest will use his finger to put some blood from the sin offering on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He’ll pour all the rest at the base of the altar.

He’ll remove all the fat, just like with a lamb brought as a peace offering. The priest will burn it on the altar, on top of the offerings given to Yahweh through fire. The priest will make atonement for what that person did, and they’ll be forgiven.’”
“‘Say someone calls publicly for witnesses to speak under oath. If you saw what happened or know something about it and keep quiet, that’s a sin. You’ll answer for it.
“‘Say you touch something unclean, like the dead body of an unclean wild animal, farm animal, or crawling creature. Even if you don’t realize you touched it, you’re unclean and guilty.
“‘Or say you come into contact with something unclean from another person, whatever made them unclean. You didn’t notice at the time. Once you find out, you’re guilty.
“‘Or say you blurt out an oath to do something bad or good. Whatever you swore in the heat of the moment, if you didn’t realize it at the time, you’re guilty when you find out.
If you’re guilty of any of these things, own up to exactly what you did.
Bring Yahweh a guilt offering for that sin: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for what you did.
“‘Can’t afford a lamb? Bring Yahweh two turtledoves or two young pigeons as your guilt offering. One is for a sin offering and the other is for a burnt offering.
Take both to the priest. He’ll offer the bird for the sin offering first. He’ll wring its head at the neck, keeping it attached.
He’ll sprinkle some of the blood against the side of the altar and drain the rest at its base. That’s the sin offering.
He’ll offer the second bird as a burnt offering, following the rules for it. The priest will make atonement for what you did, and you’ll be forgiven.
“‘Can’t afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons? Bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering for what you did. Leave out the oil and frankincense. This is a sin offering.
Take the flour to the priest. He’ll scoop out a handful as the portion that serves as a reminder and burn it on the altar on top of the offerings given to Yahweh through fire. That’s a sin offering.
The priest will make atonement for whichever of these things you did, and you’ll be forgiven. The rest of the flour goes to the priest, just like with a grain offering.’”
Yahweh told Moses:

“If someone does wrong without realizing it in a matter involving something holy that belongs to Yahweh, bring Yahweh a ram from the flock with no defects as a guilt offering. Use your valuation in silver, measured in sanctuary shekels.
Pay back what’s owed for the wrong done to the holy thing, add a fifth, and give it to the priest. The priest will make atonement for you with the ram from the guilt offering, and you’ll be forgiven.
“If you do something Yahweh commanded you to stay away from, you’re still guilty even if you didn’t know. You’ll answer for what you did.

Bring the priest a ram from the flock with no defects as a guilt offering, according to your valuation. The priest will make atonement for the wrong you did without knowing it, and you’ll be forgiven.
That’s a guilt offering. You really were guilty before Yahweh.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Suppose someone sins against Yahweh by cheating a neighbor over something entrusted to them or over a deal, by stealing, or by taking advantage of that neighbor.
Maybe they found something that was lost and lied about it under oath. Any of those actions is a sin.
When they’re guilty of that sin, they must return what they stole, what they got by taking advantage of someone, what was left in their care, or the lost thing they found.
The same goes for anything else they lied about under oath. Pay it back in full, plus a fifth. Give it to the owner the day you’re found guilty.
Bring the priest a ram from the flock with no defects as a guilt offering to Yahweh, according to your valuation.
The priest will make atonement for that person before Yahweh, and they’ll be forgiven for whatever made them guilty.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Give Aaron and his sons these instructions: ‘Here’s the rule for the burnt offering. Leave it on the altar hearth all night till morning. Keep the altar fire going.
The priest will put on his linen clothes, including his linen trousers. He’ll clear out the ashes left after the fire burns up the offering and set them beside the altar.
Then he’ll change clothes and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
Don’t let the altar fire die out. Every morning the priest will add wood, arrange the burnt offering over the fire, and burn the fat from the peace offerings on it.
Keep that altar fire going all the time. It must never go out. 🔥
“‘Here’s the rule for the grain offering. Aaron’s sons will bring it before Yahweh at the altar.
The priest will take a handful of fine flour and oil, along with all the frankincense on the offering. He’ll burn that portion on the altar as a reminder. Its smell will be pleasing to Yahweh.
Aaron and his sons will eat what’s left, without yeast, in a holy place. They’ll eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Don’t bake it with yeast. I’ve given it to them as their share of my offerings given through fire. It’s most holy, just like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male descendant of Aaron may eat it. That share of Yahweh’s offerings given through fire is theirs for every generation. Whoever touches these offerings will be holy.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Here’s what Aaron and his sons will offer Yahweh, starting on the day of anointing: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
Prepare it with oil on a griddle. Bring it in once it’s soaked, and offer it in baked pieces so its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
The anointed priest who takes Aaron’s place from among his sons will make this offering. Burn the whole thing for Yahweh. That rule stands forever.
Burn every grain offering a priest brings in full. Nobody is to eat any of it.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron and his sons this: ‘Here’s the rule for the sin offering. Slaughter it before Yahweh where you slaughter the burnt offering. It’s most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin will eat it in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Whatever touches its meat will be holy. If blood spatters onto any clothing, wash the spot in a holy place.
If you boil the meat in a clay pot, break the pot. If you boil it in a bronze pot, scrub it and rinse it with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It’s most holy.
If any blood from a sin offering goes into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, nobody may eat that offering. Burn it up.’”
“‘Here’s the rule for the guilt offering. It’s most holy.
Slaughter it where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
Offer all its fat, including the fat tail and the fat covering the insides.
Take out both kidneys and the fat on them near the lower back. Remove the piece that covers the liver along with the kidneys.
The priest will burn those parts on the altar as an offering given to Yahweh through fire. That’s the guilt offering.
Any male among the priests may eat it. Eat it in a holy place. It’s most holy.
“‘The same rule applies to the sin offering and the guilt offering. It goes to the priest who makes atonement with it.
When a priest offers someone’s burnt offering, the hide of the animal he offered is his to keep.
Any grain offering baked in the oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle goes to the priest who offers it.
Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all of Aaron’s sons. They share it equally.
“‘Here’s the rule for a peace offering someone brings to Yahweh.
If you’re bringing it to give thanks, bring cakes without yeast mixed with oil, thin wafers without yeast brushed with oil, and cakes mixed with oil.
Bring cakes of bread made with yeast too, alongside your peace offering of thanks.
Take one from each kind and lift it up as an offering to Yahweh. It goes to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offering.
Eat the meat from your peace offering of thanks on the day you offer it. Don’t keep any till morning.
“‘If you’re making the sacrifice to keep a vow or you’re giving it freely, eat it on the day you offer it. Eat what’s left the next day.
By the third day, whatever meat is still left must be burned. 🔥
If anyone eats the meat on day three, the peace offering won’t be accepted or credited to the person who brought it. It’s detestable, and whoever eats it will answer for what they did.
“‘If any meat touches something unclean, burn it. Don’t eat it. As for the rest of the meat, anyone who’s clean may eat it.
If someone who’s unclean eats meat from a peace offering that belongs to Yahweh, that person will be cut off from their people.

If anyone touches something unclean, whether it comes from a person, an unclean animal, or anything unclean and detestable, and then eats meat from Yahweh’s peace offering, that person will be cut off from their people.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites this: ‘Don’t eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
If an animal dies on its own or is torn apart by another animal, you can use its fat for other things. Don’t eat any of it.
Anyone who eats fat from the kind of animal people offer to Yahweh through fire will be cut off from their people.
Don’t eat blood from any bird or animal, wherever you live.
Whoever eats any blood will be cut off from their people.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites this: ‘When someone brings a peace offering to Yahweh, they must bring Yahweh his share from that sacrifice.
Bring what’s to be offered to Yahweh through fire with your own hands. Bring the fat along with the breast, so the breast can be waved as an offering before Yahweh.
The priest will burn the fat on the altar. The breast goes to Aaron and his sons.
Give the priest the right thigh from your peace offering as an offering lifted up.
The right thigh goes to the son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the peace offering.
I’ve taken the waved breast and the lifted thigh from the Israelites’ peace offerings and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. That’s their share from Israel forever.’”
These are the portions set apart for Aaron and his sons from Yahweh’s offerings given through fire when they were presented to serve Yahweh as priests.
On the day he anointed them, Yahweh told the Israelites to give them those portions. The portions belong to them for every generation.
Those are the rules for burnt offerings, grain offerings, sin offerings, guilt offerings, offerings for setting priests apart, and peace offerings.
Yahweh gave Moses these rules on Mount Sinai when he told the Israelites to bring their offerings to him in the Sinai wilderness.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Bring Aaron and his sons, the clothes, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread made without yeast.
Get the whole community together at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.”
Moses did what Yahweh told him, and the community gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Moses told everyone, “Here’s what Yahweh has told us to do.”
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on Aaron and tied the sash around him. Then he put the robe and the ephod on him and fastened the ephod with its expertly woven band.
He put the breastplate on Aaron and tucked the Urim and Thummim inside it.
He set the turban on Aaron’s head and put the gold plate, the holy crown, on the front, just as Yahweh had told him.
Moses took the anointing oil and used it to set apart the tabernacle and everything in it as holy.
He sprinkled the altar with the oil seven times. He anointed the altar, all its utensils, and the basin and its stand to set them apart as holy.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head to anoint him and set him apart as holy.
Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, put tunics on them, tied their sashes, and put headbands on them, just as Yahweh had told him.
Moses brought the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.

Moses slaughtered the bull. He used his finger to put blood on the horns all around the altar, making the altar clean. He poured the rest at the base, setting the altar apart as holy to make atonement for it.
Moses took all the fat attached to the insides, the piece covering the liver, and both kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
He burned the rest of the bull outside the camp, including its hide, meat, and dung, just as Yahweh had told him.
Moses brought forward the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it and splashed its blood against all sides of the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

He rinsed the insides and legs with water, then burned the whole ram on the altar. That was a burnt offering with a pleasing smell, an offering given to Yahweh through fire, just as Yahweh had told him.
Then Moses brought forward the other ram, the one for setting the priests apart. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it and put some of its blood on the tip of Aaron’s right ear, his right thumb, and his right big toe.
Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward. He put blood on the tip of each man’s right ear, on his right thumb, and on his right big toe. Moses splashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat attached to the insides, the piece covering the liver, both kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of bread without yeast that was before Yahweh, he took one cake without yeast, one cake made with oil, and one wafer. He put them on top of the fat and the right thigh.
He put it all in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved it as an offering before Yahweh.
Moses took it back from their hands and burned it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. It was an offering to set them apart, given to Yahweh through fire, with a pleasing smell.
Moses took the breast and waved it as an offering before Yahweh. That was his share of the ram for setting the priests apart, just as Yahweh had told him.
Moses took some of the anointing oil and some blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron, his sons, and all their clothes. He set them and their clothes apart as holy.

Moses told Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Eat it there with the bread from the basket for setting you apart, just as I said when I gave the order, ‘Aaron and his sons will eat it.’
Burn whatever meat and bread is left over. 🔥
Stay at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for seven days, till your time of being set apart is done. It takes seven days to set you apart.
What you saw done today is what Yahweh commanded to make atonement for you.
Stay at that entrance day and night for all seven days. Do what Yahweh says so you don’t die. That’s what he told me to say.”
Aaron and his sons did everything Yahweh had told them through Moses.
On day eight, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and Israel’s elders together.
He told Aaron, “Take a calf from the herd for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Both must be free of defects. Offer them before Yahweh.
Tell the Israelites, ‘Bring a male goat for a sin offering. For a burnt offering, bring a calf and a lamb, each a year old and free of defects.
Bring a bull and a ram to sacrifice as peace offerings before Yahweh, and bring a grain offering mixed with oil. Today Yahweh is going to appear to you.’”
They brought everything Moses had asked for to the front of the Tent of Meeting. The whole community came forward and stood before Yahweh.
Moses said, “Do what Yahweh has commanded, and you’ll see his glory.”

Moses told Aaron, “Go up to the altar. Give your sin offering and burnt offering to make atonement for yourself and the people. Then bring the people’s offering and make atonement for them, just as Yahweh told us.”
Aaron went up to the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering.
His sons handed him the blood. He dipped his finger in it and put some on the horns of the altar, then poured the blood out at its base.
He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the piece covering the liver on the altar, just as Yahweh had told Moses.
He took the meat and the hide outside the camp and burned them there.
Aaron slaughtered the animal for the burnt offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar.
They handed him the pieces and the head, and he burned them on the altar.
He washed the insides and legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
Then Aaron brought the people’s offering. He took the goat for their sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it for their sin the same way he’d offered the first one.
He brought the burnt offering and followed the rules for offering it.
He brought the grain offering, scooped up a handful, and burned it on the altar in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.
Aaron slaughtered the bull and the ram for the people’s peace offerings. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar.
They also brought the fat from the bull and the ram, including the fat tail, the fat covering the insides, the kidneys, and the piece covering the liver.
They laid the fat on top of the breasts, and Aaron burned the fat on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before Yahweh as a wave offering, just as Moses had commanded.
Aaron raised his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down after making the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting. When they came back out, they blessed the people, and everyone saw Yahweh’s glory.
Fire came from before Yahweh and burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. 🔥 When the people saw it, they shouted and fell facedown.
Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu each took his incense burner, put fire in it, and laid incense on top. They brought fire before Yahweh that he hadn’t told them to offer.
Fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed them. They died there before him.
Moses told Aaron, “This is what Yahweh meant when he said, ‘I’ll show those who come near me that I am holy. Before all the people, I’ll be glorified.’” Aaron stayed silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel. “Come here,” he said. “Carry your relatives away from the front of the sanctuary and out of the camp.”
They came over and carried them out of the camp in their tunics, just as Moses had said.

Moses told Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Don’t let your hair hang loose or tear your clothes. If you do, you’ll die and Yahweh will be angry with the whole community. Let your relatives, all Israel, mourn over the fire Yahweh started.
Don’t leave the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, or you’ll die. Yahweh’s anointing oil is on you.” They did what Moses said.
Then Yahweh spoke to Aaron:
“Whenever you and your sons go into the Tent of Meeting, don’t drink wine or strong drink, or you’ll die. This rule stands for every generation.
You must tell the difference between what’s holy and what’s ordinary, and between what’s unclean and what’s clean.
Teach the Israelites all the rules Yahweh gave them through Moses.”

Moses told Aaron and his surviving sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take what’s left of the grain offering from the offerings given to Yahweh through fire. Eat it without yeast beside the altar. It’s most holy.
Eat it in a holy place. It’s your share and your sons’ share of the offerings given to Yahweh through fire. That’s what I was commanded.
You, your sons, and your daughters can eat the waved breast and the lifted thigh in a clean place. They’ve been given to you and your sons as your share from the Israelites’ peace offerings.

The people must bring the lifted thigh and the waved breast with the fat that’s offered through fire, to wave them as an offering before Yahweh. That’s your share and your sons’ share forever, just as Yahweh commanded.”
Moses asked around to find out what happened to the goat for the sin offering. It had been burned. He got angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons, and asked,
“Why didn’t you eat the sin offering in the sanctuary area? It’s most holy. Yahweh gave it to you to bear the community’s guilt and make atonement for them before him.
Look, its blood wasn’t taken into the inner part of the sanctuary. You should have eaten the offering in the sanctuary, just as I told you.”

Aaron said to Moses, “Look, today they brought their sin offering and burnt offering before Yahweh, and then all this happened to me. If I’d eaten the sin offering today, would Yahweh have been pleased?”
When Moses heard Aaron’s answer, he was satisfied.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Here’s what you can eat from all the animals on earth.
You can eat any animal that has a hoof split all the way through and chews its cud.
“‘Here are the exceptions among animals that chew their cud or have split hooves. The camel chews its cud but doesn’t have a split hoof. It’s unclean to you.
The hyrax chews its cud but doesn’t have a split hoof. It’s unclean to you.
The hare chews its cud but doesn’t have a split hoof. It’s unclean to you.
The pig has a hoof split all the way through but doesn’t chew its cud. It’s unclean to you.
Don’t eat their meat or touch their dead bodies. They’re unclean to you.
“‘Here’s what you can eat from the water: anything with fins and scales, whether it lives in the sea or in a river.
Treat every creature in the seas and rivers that lacks fins and scales as detestable. That goes for everything that moves or lives in the water.
Treat them as detestable. Don’t eat their meat, and detest their dead bodies too.
Anything in the water without fins or scales is detestable to you.
“‘Here are the birds you must treat as detestable. Don’t eat them: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, every kind of black kite,
every kind of raven,
the horned owl, the screech owl, the gull, every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
“‘Every flying insect that walks on all fours is detestable to you.
There’s an exception you can eat: winged creatures that walk on all fours and have long, jointed legs for hopping on the ground.
That includes every kind of locust, katydid, cricket, and grasshopper.
All other winged creatures that crawl on four feet are detestable to you.
“‘Here’s how these creatures can make you unclean. Touch a dead one and you’ll be unclean until evening.
If you carry any part of its dead body, wash your clothes. You’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘Any animal whose hoof isn’t split all the way through or that doesn’t chew its cud is unclean to you. Anyone who touches one becomes unclean.
Any animal that walks on all fours on paws is unclean to you. Touch its dead body and you’ll be unclean until evening.
Carry its dead body and you’ll have to wash your clothes. You’ll be unclean until evening. These animals are unclean to you.
“‘Of the creatures that crawl on the ground, these are unclean to you: the weasel, the rat, every kind of large lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are the crawling creatures that are unclean to you. Anyone who touches one of them dead will be unclean until evening.

If one of them dies and falls on something, that thing becomes unclean. Whether it’s a wooden container, clothing, leather, a sack, or any other object you use for work, put it in water. It stays unclean until evening. After that it’s clean.
If one falls inside a clay pot, the pot and everything in it become unclean. Break the pot.
Any food that’s normally safe to eat becomes unclean if it’s soaked with that water. Anything drinkable in such a container becomes unclean too.
Anything a piece of their dead body falls on becomes unclean. If it lands on an oven or a cooking stand, smash it. Those things are unclean, and you must treat them that way.
A spring or a cistern where water collects stays clean. Anything that touches their dead bodies becomes unclean.
If a piece of their dead body falls on seed meant for planting, the seed stays clean.
But if the seed has been watered and a piece falls on it, the seed is unclean to you.
“‘If an animal you’re allowed to eat dies, anyone who touches its dead body is unclean until evening.
Anyone who eats from its dead body must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries it must wash their clothes too and will be unclean until evening.
“‘Every creature that crawls on the ground is detestable. Don’t eat it.
Whether it travels on its belly, on all fours, or on lots of feet, don’t eat any of these creatures that crawl on the ground. They’re detestable.
Don’t make yourselves detestable by means of any crawling creature. Don’t let them make you unclean and defile you.
I’m Yahweh your God. Set yourselves apart and be holy, because I’m holy. Don’t defile yourselves with any crawling creature that moves along the ground.
I’m Yahweh, the one who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. So be holy, because I’m holy.
“‘That’s the rule for animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every creature that crawls on the ground.
Use it to tell what’s clean and what’s unclean, and which creatures you can eat and which you can’t.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites this: ‘If a woman gets pregnant and gives birth to a boy, she’ll be unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
On day eight, circumcise the boy.
She’ll spend thirty-three more days going through purification from the bleeding. Until that time is up, she must stay out of the sanctuary and keep her hands off anything holy.
If she gives birth to a girl, she’ll be unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. She’ll spend sixty-six more days going through purification from the bleeding.

“‘When her time of purification is up, whether she had a son or a daughter, she’ll bring a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering. She’ll bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
He’ll present the offering before Yahweh and make atonement for her. Then she’ll be clean from the flow of blood. This is the rule for anyone who gives birth, whether to a boy or to a girl.

If she can’t afford a lamb, she’ll bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for her, and she’ll be clean.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“If someone gets a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot on their skin and it develops into a sore that looks like leprosy, bring them to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who serves as a priest.
The priest will check the sore. If the hair in it has turned white and the sore looks deeper than the skin, it’s leprosy. After examining the person, the priest will declare them unclean.
If the spot is white but looks no deeper than the skin and the hair hasn’t turned white, the priest will keep the person apart for seven days.
On day seven the priest will look again. If the sore looks the same to him and hasn’t spread, he’ll keep the person apart for another seven days.
On the next seventh day, the priest will look again. If the sore has faded and hasn’t spread across the skin, he’ll declare the person clean. It’s a scab. They’ll wash their clothes and be clean.
If the scab spreads after the person has already been to the priest to be declared clean, they’ll go back and show him again.
The priest will check. If the scab has spread, he’ll declare the person unclean. It’s leprosy.
“If someone develops a sore from leprosy, bring them to the priest.
He’ll check the person for a white swelling that has turned the hair white and has raw flesh in it.
That’s a lasting case of leprosy in the skin. The priest will declare them unclean right away. There’s no need to keep them apart for observation because they’re already unclean.
“If leprosy breaks out everywhere and covers the person from head to toe, as far as the priest can see,
the priest will check them. If it covers their whole body, he’ll declare them clean of the disease. Their skin has all turned white, so they’re clean.
Whenever raw flesh appears, that person is unclean.
The priest will look at the raw flesh and declare the person unclean. Raw flesh is unclean. It’s leprosy.
If the raw flesh turns white again, the person will go back to the priest.
The priest will check them. If the sore has turned white, he’ll declare the person clean of the disease. They’re clean.
“Say someone had a boil on their skin and it healed,
but a white swelling or a bright reddish-white spot shows up where the boil was. Show it to the priest.
He’ll check it. If the spot looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it has turned white, he’ll declare the person unclean. It’s leprosy that broke out where the boil was.
If the priest sees no white hair in it, and the spot is faded and goes no deeper than the skin, he’ll keep the person apart for seven days.
If it spreads across the skin, the priest will declare them unclean. It’s a diseased sore.
If the bright spot stays where it was and doesn’t spread, it’s the scar from the boil. The priest will declare the person clean.
“Say someone burns their skin with fire, and the raw flesh of the burn turns into a shiny spot that’s reddish-white or white.

The priest will check it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot looks deeper than the skin, leprosy has broken out in the burn. The priest will declare the person unclean. It’s leprosy.
If the priest sees no white hair in the spot, and it’s faded and goes no deeper than the skin, he’ll keep the person apart for seven days.
The priest will check again on day seven. If the spot has spread across the skin, he’ll declare the person unclean. It’s leprosy.
If the spot stays where it was, hasn’t spread, and has faded, it’s the swelling from the burn. The priest will declare the person clean because it’s a burn scar.
“If a man or woman gets a sore on the scalp or in the beard area,

the priest will look at the sore. If it looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it is thin and yellow, he’ll declare the person unclean. It’s an itchy sore, a case of leprosy on the scalp or beard.
If the priest checks the itchy sore and it looks no deeper than the skin but has no black hair in it, he’ll keep the person apart for seven days.
On day seven the priest will check it again. If it hasn’t spread, has no yellow hair in it, and looks no deeper than the skin,
the person will shave around the sore, leaving the sore itself unshaved. The priest will keep them apart for another seven days.
On the next seventh day the priest will check it. If it hasn’t spread and looks no deeper than the skin, he’ll declare the person clean. They’ll wash their clothes and be clean.
If the sore spreads after the person has been declared clean,
the priest will check again. If it’s spread across the skin, there’s no need to look for yellow hair. The person is unclean.
If the priest sees that it has stopped spreading and black hair has grown in it, the sore has healed. The person is clean, and the priest will say so.
“If a man or woman gets bright white spots on their skin,
the priest will check them. If the spots are dull white, it’s a harmless rash that broke out on the skin. The person is clean.
“If a man loses the hair on his head, he’s bald and he’s clean.
If the hair falls out at the front of his head, he’s bald there and he’s clean.
But if a reddish-white sore shows up anywhere on the bald area, leprosy is breaking out there.
The priest will check him. If the swelling on his bald scalp or forehead is reddish-white, like leprosy elsewhere on the body,
the man has leprosy and is unclean. The priest must declare him unclean. The sore is on his head.
“The person with leprosy will wear torn clothes and let their hair hang loose. They’ll cover their upper lip and call out, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’
They’ll stay unclean as long as they have the disease. They’ll live alone outside the camp.
“Now say the same kind of plague shows up on a wool or linen garment,
in the threads running lengthwise or across the cloth, in wool or linen, or in leather or something made of leather.
If the affected spot looks greenish or reddish on the garment, the leather, the lengthwise or crosswise threads, or anything made of leather, it’s a plague like leprosy. Show it to the priest.
The priest will check the spot and set the item aside for seven days.

On day seven he’ll look again. If it’s spread on the garment, in the lengthwise or crosswise threads, or on the leather, whatever the leather is used for, it’s destructive mildew. The item is unclean.
Burn the garment, the affected wool or linen threads, or the leather item where the spot appears. It’s destructive mildew. Burn it up. 🔥
“If the priest checks it and the spot hasn’t spread on the garment, in either direction of the weave, or on the leather,
he’ll order the item washed and set it aside for another seven days.

The priest will check the spot after it’s been washed. If its color is the same, even if it hasn’t spread, it’s unclean. Burn it. The spot is mildew, whether it’s eaten into the inside or the outside.
If the priest sees that the spot has faded after washing, he’ll tear it out of the garment, the leather, or the lengthwise or crosswise threads.
If the spot shows up again on the garment, in the threads, or on anything made of leather, it’s spreading. Burn whatever has the spot.
If washing takes the spot out of the garment, out of the threads, or off the leather, wash it a second time, and it’ll be clean.”
That’s the rule for deciding whether wool, linen, the threads running either way in the cloth, or anything made of leather is clean or unclean when mildew shows up.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Here’s the rule for the day someone with leprosy is to be made clean. Bring the person to the priest.
The priest will go outside the camp and examine them there. If their leprosy has healed,
he’ll tell the people to get two live, clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop for the person being made clean.
The priest will tell them to slaughter one bird in a clay pot over running water.
He’ll take the live bird, the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn, and the hyssop and dip them in the blood of the bird killed over the running water.
He’ll sprinkle the person being cleansed from leprosy seven times and declare them clean. Then he’ll let the live bird fly away into the open field.

“The person being made clean will wash their clothes, shave off all their hair, and bathe in water. Then they’ll be clean. They can come back into camp, but they must stay outside their tent for seven days.
On day seven they’ll shave all their hair, including their head, beard, and eyebrows. Shave it all off. Then they’ll wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they’ll be clean.

“On day eight they’ll bring two male lambs with no defects and one year-old female lamb with no defects. They’ll also bring three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who performs the cleansing will present the person and these offerings before Yahweh at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
“The priest will take one of the male lambs and the log of oil for a guilt offering and wave them before Yahweh as a wave offering.
He’ll slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin and burnt offerings are slaughtered. The guilt offering belongs to the priest, just like the sin offering. It’s most holy.
The priest will put some blood from the guilt offering on the tip of the person’s right ear, on their right thumb, and on their right big toe.
The priest will pour some of the log of oil into his own left palm.
He’ll dip a finger of his right hand in the oil in his left palm and sprinkle some of it seven times before Yahweh.
He’ll put some of the oil left in his palm on the tip of the person’s right ear, their right thumb, and their right big toe, right over the blood from the guilt offering.
The priest will put the rest of the oil in his palm on the head of the person being cleansed. He’ll make atonement for them before Yahweh.
“The priest will make the sin offering to make atonement for the person’s uncleanness. After that he’ll slaughter the burnt offering.
Then he’ll put the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. The priest will make atonement for the person, and they’ll be clean.

“If the person is poor and can’t afford all that, here’s what they’ll bring: one male lamb to be waved as a guilt offering to make atonement for them, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil.
They’ll also bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever they can afford. One is for a sin offering and the other is for a burnt offering.
“On day eight they’ll bring these for their cleansing to the priest before Yahweh, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will take the lamb for the guilt offering and the log of oil and wave them before Yahweh as a wave offering.
He’ll slaughter the lamb for the guilt offering. Then he’ll put some of its blood on the tip of the person’s right ear, on their right thumb, and on their right big toe.
The priest will pour some of the oil into his own left palm.
He’ll use a finger of his right hand to sprinkle some of the oil from his left palm seven times before Yahweh.
The priest will put some of the oil in his palm on the tip of the person’s right ear, their right thumb, and their right big toe, where he put the blood from the guilt offering.
He’ll put the rest of the oil in his palm on the person’s head to make atonement for them before Yahweh.
Then he’ll offer the birds the person could afford, whether turtledoves or young pigeons:
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, along with the grain offering. The priest will make atonement before Yahweh for the person being cleansed.”
That’s the rule for people with leprosy who can’t afford the usual sacrifice for their cleansing.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“When you get to Canaan, the land I’m giving you to own, and I cause mildew to spread in a house in that land,
the homeowner must tell the priest, ‘It looks like something’s spreading in my house.’
Before he goes in to check the affected area, the priest will tell them to clear the house so everything inside won’t become unclean. Then he’ll go in and look.
He’ll check the affected area. If the walls have greenish or reddish streaks that look sunken below the surface,
the priest will go out to the doorway and close up the house for seven days.
On day seven the priest will come back and look. If the affected area has spread across the walls,
he’ll tell them to pull out the affected stones and dump them in an unclean place outside the city.
He’ll have the whole inside of the house scraped. They’ll dump the plaster they scraped off in an unclean place outside the city.
They’ll put new stones where the old ones were and replaster the house with fresh mortar.
“If the mildew breaks out again after the stones have been taken out and the house has been scraped and replastered,
the priest will go in and take a look. If the patch has spread, it’s destructive mildew. The house is unclean.
Tear down the house, stones, beams, plaster and all. Carry the debris to an unclean place outside the city.
“Anyone who goes inside while the house is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who lies down or eats in the house must wash their clothes.
“If the priest goes back to check the house after it’s been replastered and the affected area hasn’t spread, he’ll declare the house clean because the mildew is gone.
To cleanse the house, he’ll take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
He’ll slaughter one bird in a clay pot over running water.
He’ll take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the live bird and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the running water. Then he’ll sprinkle the house seven times.
He’ll cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the running water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
Then he’ll let the live bird go outside the city into the open field. That’s how he’ll make atonement for the house, and it’ll be clean.”
These are the rules for sores from leprosy and for itchy sores,
for destructive mildew on clothing or in a house,
and for swellings, scabs, and bright spots.
They show when something is unclean and when it’s clean. That’s the law of leprosy.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Tell the Israelites this: ‘If a man has a discharge from his body, that discharge makes him unclean.
Whether it’s flowing or his body has stopped it up, either way he’s unclean.
“‘Any bed he lies on and anything he sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits where he sat must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘Anyone who touches the man himself must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘If the man spits on someone who’s clean, that person must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘Any saddle the man rides on becomes unclean.
Touch anything that was under him and you’ll be unclean until evening. If you carry any of those things, you must wash your clothes and bathe in water, and you’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘If the man touches someone before rinsing his hands in water, that person must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘Break any clay pot the man touches. Rinse every wooden container he touches in water.
“‘Once his discharge clears up, he’ll count off seven days for his cleansing. Then he’ll wash his clothes and bathe in running water, and he’ll be clean.
“‘On day eight he’ll bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons before Yahweh at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and hand them to the priest.
The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest will make atonement for him before Yahweh for his discharge.
“‘If a man releases semen, he must bathe his whole body in water. He’ll be unclean until evening.
Wash any clothing or leather that gets semen on it. It’ll be unclean until evening.
If a man sleeps with a woman and releases semen, both of them must bathe in water, and both will be unclean until evening.
“‘When a woman has a discharge of blood from her body, she’ll be unclean for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
“‘While she’s unclean, anything she lies down on or sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches something she’s been sitting on must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They’ll be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches something on her bed or on whatever she sits on will be unclean until evening.
“‘If a man sleeps with her and gets her menstrual blood on him, he’ll be unclean for seven days. Any bed he lies on will be unclean too.
“‘If a woman bleeds for many days outside her period, or the bleeding goes on past her period, she’ll be unclean the whole time she bleeds, just as she is during her period.
Every bed she lies on while she’s bleeding is treated like the bed she uses during her period. Anything she sits on becomes unclean, just as it does during her period.
Anyone who touches those things becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they’ll be unclean until evening.
“‘When the bleeding stops, she’ll count off seven days. After that she’ll be clean.
On day eight she’ll take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest will make atonement for her before Yahweh for the uncleanness from her discharge.
“‘This is how you’ll keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so they don’t die in it by defiling my tabernacle, which is right there among them.’”
These are the rules for a man with a discharge or a release of semen that makes him unclean,
for a woman on her period, for a man or woman with a discharge, and for a man who sleeps with a woman while she’s unclean.
Yahweh spoke to Moses after Aaron’s two sons came near to Yahweh and died.

Yahweh said, “Tell your brother Aaron he can’t just walk behind the curtain into the Most Holy Place whenever he wants. If he comes before the mercy seat on top of the ark like that, he’ll die, because I’ll appear in the cloud over the mercy seat.
“Here’s how Aaron is to enter the sanctuary: bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
He’ll bathe in water and put on the holy linen clothes: the tunic, the trousers, the sash, and the turban.
He’ll take two male goats from the Israelite community for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
“Aaron will present the bull for his own sin offering to make atonement for himself and his household.
He’ll take both goats and stand them before Yahweh at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron will draw lots for the goats, one for Yahweh and the other for the scapegoat.
He’ll bring forward the goat picked for Yahweh and offer it as a sin offering.
The goat picked as the scapegoat will be presented alive before Yahweh so atonement can be made over it. Then it’ll be sent away into the wilderness as the scapegoat.
“Aaron will bring forward the bull for his own sin offering, make atonement for himself and his household, and slaughter the bull for his sin offering.
He’ll fill an incense burner with burning coals from the altar before Yahweh and take two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense. He’ll bring them behind the curtain.
He’ll put the incense on the coals before Yahweh so the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat above the covenant. That way he won’t die.
He’ll use his finger to sprinkle some of the bull’s blood on the east side of the mercy seat. Then he’ll sprinkle some in front of it seven times with his finger.
“Then he’ll slaughter the goat for the people’s sin offering and take its blood behind the curtain. He’ll do what he did with the bull’s blood, sprinkling it on the mercy seat and in front of it.

He’ll make atonement for the Holy Place because of the Israelites’ uncleanness, their rebellion, and all their sins. He’ll do the same for the Tent of Meeting, which stands right there among them in the middle of their uncleanness.

Nobody else can be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out, after making atonement for himself, his household, and the whole Israelite community.
“He’ll go out to the altar that stands before Yahweh and make atonement for it. He’ll put some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood on the horns all around the altar.
He’ll sprinkle blood on it seven times with his finger, cleansing it from the Israelites’ uncleanness and setting it apart as holy.
“When he’s finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he’ll bring the live goat forward.

Aaron will put both hands on the live goat’s head and confess over it all the wrongs, rebellion, and sins of the Israelites. He’ll put those sins on the goat’s head and hand the goat over to someone ready to take it into the wilderness.
The goat will carry all their wrongs on itself to a place where nobody lives. The man will let it go in the wilderness.
“Aaron will go into the Tent of Meeting and take off the linen clothes he wore into the Holy Place. He’ll leave them there.
He’ll bathe in water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he’ll come out and make his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering to make atonement for himself and the people.
He’ll burn the fat from the sin offering on the altar.
“The man who lets the scapegoat go must wash his clothes and bathe in water before coming back into camp.
Take the bull and goat for the sin offerings out of camp. Their blood was taken into the Holy Place to make atonement. Burn their hides, meat, and dung there.
Whoever burns them must wash their clothes and bathe in water before coming back into camp.
“Here’s a rule for you to keep forever. On the tenth day of the seventh month, humble yourselves and do no work at all. That goes for everyone born among you and for foreigners living with you.
On that day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you. You’ll be clean before Yahweh from all your sins.
This is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you’ll humble yourselves. That rule stands forever.
The priest anointed and set apart to take his father’s place will make atonement. He’ll put on the holy linen clothes.
He’ll make atonement for the Holy Sanctuary, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar. He’ll also make atonement for the priests and everyone in the community.
“Keep this rule forever: once a year, make atonement for the Israelites for all their sins.” It was done just as Yahweh told Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, ‘Here’s what Yahweh has commanded:
Suppose someone from Israel slaughters a bull, a lamb, or a goat, whether inside the camp or outside it,

and doesn’t bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to give it to Yahweh as an offering in front of his tabernacle. That person is guilty of shedding blood. They shed blood and will be cut off from their people.

The point is for the Israelites to bring the sacrifices they’ve been making out in the open fields to Yahweh. Bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and offer them there to Yahweh as peace offerings.
The priest will splash the blood on Yahweh’s altar at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat so its smell is pleasing to Yahweh.
They must stop sacrificing to the goat idols they’ve been chasing after like unfaithful partners. This rule stands for every generation.’
“Tell them, ‘If an Israelite or a foreigner living among them offers a burnt offering or any other sacrifice,
and doesn’t bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to offer it to Yahweh, that person will be cut off from their people.
“‘If anyone from Israel or any foreigner living among them eats blood of any kind, I’ll turn against that person and cut them off from their people.
The life of the body is in the blood. I’ve given you the blood to use on the altar to make atonement for your lives. The blood makes atonement because of the life in it.
That’s why I told the Israelites, “Nobody among you may eat blood. No foreigner living among you may eat it either.”
“‘If an Israelite or a foreigner living among them hunts and catches an animal or bird you’re allowed to eat, they must drain its blood and cover it with dirt.
The blood of every creature goes with its life. That’s why I told the Israelites, “Don’t eat the blood of any creature. The blood is its life. Whoever eats it will be cut off.”

“‘Anyone who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn apart by other animals must wash their clothes and bathe in water. That goes for someone born among you or a foreigner. They’ll be unclean until evening, and then they’ll be clean.
If they skip washing their clothes or bathing, they’ll answer for what they did.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘I’m Yahweh your God.
Don’t copy what people do in Egypt, where you used to live, or in Canaan, where I’m taking you. Don’t live by their rules.
Follow my instructions. Keep my laws and live by them. I’m Yahweh your God.
Keep my laws and my instructions. Whoever follows them will live by them. I’m Yahweh.
“‘None of you may approach a close relative to uncover their nakedness. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Don’t uncover your father’s nakedness or your mother’s. She’s your mother. Don’t uncover her nakedness.
“‘Don’t uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife. That’s your father’s nakedness.
“‘Don’t uncover your sister’s nakedness, whether she’s your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether she was born at home or somewhere else.
“‘Don’t uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter. Their nakedness is your own.
“‘Don’t uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter if your father is her father too. She’s your sister.
“‘Don’t uncover your father’s sister’s nakedness. She’s his close relative.
“‘Don’t uncover your mother’s sister’s nakedness. She’s your mother’s close relative.
“‘Don’t uncover your father’s brother’s nakedness by approaching his wife. She’s your aunt.
“‘Don’t uncover your daughter-in-law’s nakedness. She’s your son’s wife. Don’t uncover her nakedness.
“‘Don’t uncover your brother’s wife’s nakedness. That’s your brother’s nakedness.
“‘Don’t uncover the nakedness of both a woman and her daughter. Don’t take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover her nakedness either. They’re close relatives. That’s wicked.
“‘While your wife is still alive, don’t take her sister as a rival wife and uncover her nakedness.
“‘Don’t approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while she’s unclean from her period.
“‘Don’t sleep with your neighbor’s wife and make yourself unclean with her.
“‘Don’t give any of your children as a sacrifice to Molech. Don’t dishonor your God’s name. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Don’t sleep with a man as you would with a woman. That’s detestable.
“‘Don’t sleep with an animal and make yourself unclean with it. A woman must never give herself to an animal to sleep with it. That’s a perversion.
“‘Don’t make yourselves unclean by doing any of these things. They’re what made the nations I’m driving out ahead of you unclean.
The land became unclean, so I punished it for its wrongdoing, and it threw up the people who lived there.
Keep my laws and instructions, and stay away from all these detestable practices. That goes for anyone born among you and for foreigners living with you.
The people who lived there before you did all those detestable things, and the land became unclean.
If you make the land unclean, it’ll throw you up too, just as it threw up the nation that was there before you.
“‘Whoever does any of these detestable things will be cut off from their people.
So keep my instructions. Don’t copy the detestable customs people practiced before you or make yourselves unclean by them. I’m Yahweh your God.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the whole Israelite community, ‘Be holy, because I, Yahweh your God, am holy.
“‘Every one of you must respect your mother and father and keep my Sabbaths. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Don’t turn to idols or cast metal gods for yourselves. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘When you bring Yahweh a peace offering, offer it in a way that will get you accepted.
Eat it the day you offer it or the day after. If anything is still there on day three, burn it. 🔥
If anyone eats it on day three, it’s detestable and won’t be accepted.
Anyone who eats it will answer for what they did. They’ve treated something holy to Yahweh with disrespect, and they’ll be cut off from their people.
“‘At harvest, leave the corners of your field standing. Don’t go back to pick up what the harvesters left behind.
Don’t go back through your vineyard to pick it clean or collect the grapes that fell. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Don’t steal. Don’t lie. Don’t trick each other.
“‘Don’t swear a false oath in my name and dishonor the name of your God. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Don’t take advantage of your neighbor or rob them. Don’t keep a hired worker’s pay overnight till morning.
“‘Don’t curse someone who’s deaf or put something in the way of someone who’s blind to trip them. Honor your God with reverence. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Be fair when you judge. Don’t give the poor special treatment or play favorites with powerful people. Judge your neighbor by what’s right.
“‘Don’t go around spreading lies about your own people. Don’t put your neighbor’s life in danger. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Don’t carry hate for your brother in your heart. Call your neighbor out when they do wrong, so you don’t carry sin because of them.
“‘Don’t get even or hold a grudge against anyone among your people. Love your neighbor the way you love yourself. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Keep my laws. Don’t breed two different kinds of animals together. Don’t plant two kinds of seed in the same field. Don’t wear clothes made from two kinds of material.

“‘If a man sleeps with an enslaved woman who’s promised to another man and hasn’t been bought out of slavery or given her freedom, they’ll be punished. They won’t be put to death, because she wasn’t free.
He must bring a ram to Yahweh as a guilt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will use the ram from the guilt offering to make atonement for him before Yahweh. Then the sin he committed will be forgiven.
“‘When you arrive in the land and plant trees for food, treat their fruit as off-limits for the first three years. Don’t eat any of it.
In the fourth year all the fruit will be holy, set apart to give praise to Yahweh.
In the fifth year you can eat the fruit, so the trees will yield more for you. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Don’t eat meat that still has blood in it. Don’t go in for enchantments or sorcery.
“‘Don’t cut the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
“‘Don’t cut yourselves for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Don’t dishonor your daughter by making her a prostitute, or prostitution will spread and the land will fill up with wickedness.
“‘Keep my Sabbaths and treat my sanctuary with reverence. I’m Yahweh.
“‘Stay away from mediums and wizards. Don’t go looking for them and make yourselves unclean through them. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Stand up when someone with gray hair comes before you. Honor older people and show reverence for your God. I’m Yahweh.
“‘When a foreigner settles in your land and lives among you, don’t mistreat them.
Treat the foreigner who lives among you like anyone born in your land. Love them as you love yourself, because you lived as foreigners in Egypt. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Don’t cheat when you judge a case or measure length, weight, or quantity.
Use honest scales, honest weights, and accurate measures for an ephah and a hin. I’m Yahweh your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt.
“‘Keep all my laws and all my instructions and put them into practice. I’m Yahweh.’”
Yahweh told Moses:

“Tell the Israelites this too: ‘If anyone from Israel, or any foreigner living in Israel, gives one of their children to Molech, that person must be put to death. The people of the land will stone them.
I’ll turn against that person myself and cut them off from their people, because they gave one of their children to Molech, defiling my sanctuary and dishonoring my holy name.
If the people of the land turn a blind eye when someone gives one of their children to Molech and they don’t put that person to death,
I’ll turn against that person and their family. I’ll cut them off from their people, along with everyone who follows them in being unfaithful with Molech.
“‘If someone turns to mediums and wizards and goes after them in unfaithfulness, I’ll turn against that person and cut them off from their people.
“‘Set yourselves apart and be holy, because I’m Yahweh your God.
Keep my laws and put them into practice. I’m Yahweh, the one who makes you holy.
“‘Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death. They cursed their own parent, and their blood is on their own head.
“‘If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife, his neighbor’s wife, both the man and the woman who committed adultery must be put to death.
“‘A man who sleeps with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both must be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.
“‘If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both must be put to death. They’ve committed a perversion. Their blood is on their own heads.
“‘If a man sleeps with a man as he would with a woman, both have done what is detestable. They must be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.
“‘If a man takes both a woman and her mother as wives, that’s wicked. All three must be burned so that there’s no such wickedness among you.
“‘If a man sleeps with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal too.
“‘If a woman approaches an animal and sleeps with it, put the woman and the animal to death. Their blood is on their own heads.

“‘If a man takes his sister, whether she’s his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and they see each other naked, that’s shameful. They’ll be cut off in front of their people. He uncovered his sister’s nakedness, and he’ll answer for what he did.
“‘If a man sleeps with a woman during her period and uncovers her nakedness, he’s exposed the source of her flow, and she’s uncovered the source of her blood. Both will be cut off from their people.
“‘Don’t uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister. That’s exposing a close relative. Both will answer for what they did.
If a man sleeps with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They’ll answer for their sin and die without children.
“‘If a man takes his brother’s wife, that’s unclean. He’s uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They’ll have no children.
“‘Keep all my laws and instructions and put them into practice so the land I’m bringing you to live in won’t throw you up.
Don’t copy the customs of the nation I’m driving out ahead of you. They did all these things, and that’s why I detested them.
But I told you, “You’ll inherit their land. I’ll give it to you to own, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I’m Yahweh your God, the one who separated you from the other peoples.

“‘So tell the difference between clean and unclean animals, and between clean and unclean birds. Don’t make yourselves detestable through any animal, bird, or creature crawling across the ground that I’ve marked off as unclean for you.
Be holy to me, because I, Yahweh, am holy. I’ve set you apart from the other peoples so you’ll be mine.
“‘Any man or woman who serves as a medium or a wizard must be put to death. They’ll be stoned. Their blood is on their own heads.’”
Yahweh told Moses, “Tell the priests, Aaron’s sons, ‘A priest must not make himself unclean for someone among his people who has died.
The exceptions are his closest relatives: his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother,
and his own sister if she’s a virgin and has never had a husband. For her he may make himself unclean.
As a leader among his people, he must not make himself unclean and dishonor his position.
“‘The priests must not shave their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or cut their bodies.
They must be holy to their God and honor his name. They bring Yahweh the offerings given through fire, the food of their God. That’s why they must be holy.
“‘A priest must not marry a prostitute, a woman who has been defiled, or a woman divorced from her husband. The priest is holy to his God.
Treat him as holy because he offers the food of your God. He must be holy to you, because I’m Yahweh, the one who makes you holy, and I’m holy.
“‘If a priest’s daughter dishonors herself through prostitution, she dishonors her father. She must be burned with fire.
“‘The high priest among his brothers has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been set apart to wear the sacred clothes. He must not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes.
He must not go near any dead body or make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
He must not leave the sanctuary or dishonor the sanctuary of his God, because his God’s anointing oil is on him like a crown. I’m Yahweh.
“‘He must marry a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been defiled, or a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people.
He must not dishonor his children among his people, because I’m Yahweh, the one who makes him holy.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron, ‘For every generation to come, none of your descendants who has a physical defect may come forward to offer the food of his God.
No man with a physical defect may approach, whether he’s blind, can’t walk normally, has a flattened nose or another deformity,
has an injured foot or hand,
has a hunched back, has dwarfism, has a defect in his eye, has an itchy skin disease or scabs, or has damaged testicles.
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a physical defect may approach to bring Yahweh the offerings given through fire. Because of the defect, he may not come forward to offer the food of his God.
He may still eat the food of his God, both the holy portions and the most holy portions.
He must stay away from the curtain and the altar because of his physical defect, so he doesn’t dishonor my holy places. I’m Yahweh, the one who makes them holy.’”
So Moses told Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron and his sons to keep away from the holy things the Israelites set apart for me when the priests are unclean, so they don’t dishonor my holy name. I’m Yahweh.

“Tell them, ‘For every generation to come, if one of your descendants approaches the holy things the Israelites set apart for Yahweh while that person is unclean, they’ll be cut off from my presence. I’m Yahweh.

“‘If any descendant of Aaron has leprosy or a discharge, they can’t eat the holy food until they’re clean. The same goes for anyone who touches something made unclean by a dead body, or touches a man who has released semen,
or touches a crawling creature that makes them unclean, or touches someone they can become unclean from, whatever made that person unclean.
Anyone who touches any of these things will be unclean until evening. They can’t eat the holy food without bathing in water.
Once the sun goes down, they’ll be clean. Then they can eat the holy food, because that’s their food.
They must not eat an animal that died on its own or was torn apart by other animals. That would make them unclean. I’m Yahweh.
“‘The priests must keep my charge so they don’t become guilty and die for treating it with disrespect. I’m Yahweh, the one who makes them holy.
“‘Nobody outside the priest’s household may eat the holy food. That includes a foreign visitor staying with the priest or a hired worker.
But an enslaved person a priest buys with his own money may eat it, and people born in his household may share his food.
If a priest’s daughter marries someone outside the priestly family, she can’t eat the holy portions lifted up as offerings.
But if she’s widowed or divorced, has no children, and moves back into her father’s house like when she was young, she can eat her father’s food. Nobody outside the household may eat any of it.
“‘If someone eats holy food by mistake, they must give the priest back its value plus a fifth.
The priests must not dishonor the holy things the Israelites offer to Yahweh
and bring guilt on them when they eat those holy things. I’m Yahweh, the one who makes them holy.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, ‘If an Israelite or a foreigner living in Israel brings Yahweh a burnt offering, whether to keep a vow or to give it freely,
bring a male from the cattle, sheep, or goats with no defects so you’ll be accepted.
Don’t bring any animal with a defect. It won’t be accepted on your behalf.
If someone sacrifices a peace offering to Yahweh from the herd or flock, whether to fulfill a vow or to give it freely, the animal must be sound to be accepted. It must have no defects.
Don’t bring Yahweh an animal that’s blind, injured, maimed, or has a wart, an infected spot, or a draining sore. Don’t burn any of them as an offering to Yahweh on the altar.
You can give a bull or lamb that’s misshapen or missing a part as a voluntary offering. It won’t be accepted to fulfill a vow.
Don’t offer Yahweh an animal whose testicles have been bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. Don’t do this in your land.
Don’t accept any of these animals from a foreigner and offer them as the food of your God. They’re damaged and have defects, so they won’t be accepted on your behalf.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“When a calf, lamb, or kid is born, leave it with its mother for seven days. Starting on day eight, it can be accepted as an offering given to Yahweh through fire.
Don’t slaughter a cow or a ewe and her young on the same day.
“When you bring Yahweh a sacrifice to give thanks, offer it so that you’ll be accepted.
Eat it that same day. Don’t save any of it for the morning. I’m Yahweh.
“So keep my commands and live them out. I’m Yahweh.
Don’t dishonor my holy name. I’ll be treated as holy among the Israelites. I’m Yahweh, the one who makes you holy,
the one who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I’m Yahweh.”
