Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Here are my appointed festivals. Announce them as holy gatherings. These are the times I’ve set.
“‘You can work for six days. Day seven is a Sabbath of complete rest and a holy gathering. Don’t do any work. It’s a Sabbath for Yahweh wherever you live.
“‘Here are Yahweh’s appointed festivals. Announce these holy gatherings at the times set for them.
Yahweh’s Passover is on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
On day fifteen of that same month, celebrate Yahweh’s Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day, gather for a holy assembly. Don’t do your regular work.
Bring Yahweh an offering through fire on each of the seven days. On day seven, gather for another holy assembly. Don’t do your regular work.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you get to the land I’m giving you and bring in its harvest, take a bundle of the first grain you cut to the priest.
He’ll wave the bundle before Yahweh so you’ll be accepted. The priest will wave it the day after the Sabbath.
On the day the bundle is waved, offer Yahweh a year-old male lamb with no defects as a burnt offering.
Bring two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as the grain offering, given to Yahweh through fire for a pleasing smell. Bring a quarter of a hin of wine with it as a drink offering.
Don’t eat any bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that day, when you’ve brought the offering to your God. Keep this rule for every generation, wherever you live.
“‘Start counting the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the bundle to be waved. Count seven full Sabbaths.
The day after the seventh Sabbath is day fifty. Bring Yahweh an offering of new grain that day.
Bring two loaves from your homes as a wave offering. Make them from two tenths of an ephah of fine flour and bake them with yeast. They’re the first of the harvest for Yahweh.

With the bread, bring seven year-old lambs with no defects, one young bull, and two rams. They’ll be a burnt offering to Yahweh, with their grain and drink offerings, given through fire for a smell that pleases him.
Bring one male goat for a sin offering and two year-old male lambs for a peace offering.
The priest will wave the first-harvest bread and the two lambs before Yahweh as a wave offering. They’ll be holy to Yahweh and will go to the priest.
Announce a holy gathering for that same day. Don’t do your regular work. Keep this rule for every generation, wherever you live.
“‘When you harvest your land, leave the corners of your field standing and don’t pick up what the harvesters leave behind. Leave it for the poor and for foreigners. I’m Yahweh your God.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘On day one of the seventh month, take a day of complete rest. Blow the trumpets as a reminder and come together for a holy gathering.
Don’t do your regular work. Bring Yahweh an offering through fire.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“But day ten of that seventh month is the Day of Atonement. Come together for a holy gathering, deny yourselves, and bring Yahweh an offering through fire.
Don’t do any work that day. It’s the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before Yahweh your God.
Anyone who refuses to deny themselves that day will be cut off from their people.
If anyone does any work that day, I’ll destroy that person from among their people.
Don’t do any work. Keep this rule for every generation, wherever you live.
It’ll be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you’ll deny yourselves. Start on the evening of day nine and keep the Sabbath from that evening to the next.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Starting on day fifteen of the seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Booths for Yahweh for seven days.
Come together for a holy gathering on day one. Don’t do your regular work.

For seven days, bring Yahweh an offering through fire. On day eight, come together for a holy gathering and bring another offering through fire to Yahweh. This is a solemn gathering. Don’t do your regular work.

“‘These are Yahweh’s appointed festivals, which you’ll announce as holy gatherings. Bring offerings to Yahweh through fire, including the burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its own day.
These are in addition to Yahweh’s Sabbaths, your gifts, everything you bring to fulfill your vows, and all the offerings you freely give to Yahweh.
“‘On day fifteen of the seventh month, after you’ve gathered in what the land produced, celebrate Yahweh’s festival for seven days. Day one is a day of complete rest, and so is day eight.
On day one, gather fruit from great trees, palm branches, branches from thick trees, and willows from the stream. Celebrate before Yahweh your God for seven days.
Keep this festival for Yahweh for seven days each year. It’s a rule for every generation. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
Live in temporary shelters for seven days. Everyone born in Israel must live in those shelters
so your children and their children will know that I had the Israelites live in temporary shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I’m Yahweh your God.’”
That’s how Moses announced Yahweh’s appointed festivals to the Israelites.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites to bring you pure oil from crushed olives for the lamps. Keep a lamp burning regularly.
In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain of the Testimony, Aaron will tend it before Yahweh from evening till morning, night after night. Keep this rule for every generation.
He’ll keep the lamps on the pure gold lampstand in order before Yahweh continually.
“Take fine flour and bake twelve cakes. Use two tenths of an ephah for each cake.
Lay them out in two rows of six on the pure gold table before Yahweh.
Put pure frankincense on each row. It’ll serve as a reminder for the bread, an offering given to Yahweh through fire.
Aaron will arrange the bread before Yahweh every Sabbath, week after week. It’s a lasting covenant on behalf of the Israelites.
The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons. They’ll eat it in a holy place because it’s their most holy share of the offerings given to Yahweh through fire. That rule stands forever.”
A man with an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites. He and an Israelite man got into a fight in the camp.
The man with the Israelite mother spoke against the Name and cursed, so they brought him to Moses. His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
They held him in custody until Yahweh made his will clear to them.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Take the man who cursed outside the camp. Everyone who heard him will put their hands on his head, and the whole community will stone him.
Tell the Israelites, ‘Anyone who curses their God will answer for their sin.

Anyone who speaks against Yahweh’s name must be put to death. The whole community must stone that person. The same goes for a foreigner or someone born among you. Whoever speaks against the Name must be put to death.
“‘Anyone who strikes and kills another person must be put to death.
Anyone who strikes and kills an animal must make it right, life for life.
If someone injures their neighbor, give them back the injury they caused:
broken bone for broken bone, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. The same injury they caused will be done to them.
Whoever kills an animal must make it right. Whoever kills a person must be put to death.
Use the same law for foreigners and for people born among you. I’m Yahweh your God.’”
Moses told the Israelites what Yahweh had said. They took the man who cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did what Yahweh had told Moses.
Yahweh spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you get to the land I’m giving you, give the land a Sabbath for Yahweh.
For six years, plant your fields, trim your vines, and bring in what they produce.
In year seven the land gets a Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath for Yahweh. Don’t plant your fields or trim your vines.
Don’t harvest what grows on its own or gather grapes from vines you haven’t trimmed. Give the land a whole year of rest.
What the land produces during its Sabbath will feed you, your male and female servants, your hired workers, and the foreigners living with you.
Everything the land produces will also feed your livestock and the animals in your land.
“‘Count off seven Sabbath years, seven times seven years. That adds up to forty-nine years.
On day ten of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement, blast the trumpet so it sounds throughout your land. 📯
Set apart year fifty as holy and announce freedom to everyone living in the land. It’s your Jubilee. Each of you will go back to your own property and your family.
The fiftieth year is your Jubilee. Don’t plant crops that year, harvest what grows on its own, or gather grapes from vines you haven’t trimmed.
It’s the Jubilee, and it’s holy to you. Eat what the field produces right out of the field.
“‘In the Year of Jubilee, each of you will go back to your own property.
“‘When you sell something to your neighbor or buy something from them, don’t cheat each other.
Set the purchase price by how many years have passed since the Jubilee. Your neighbor is selling you the harvests for the years that remain.
If there are lots of years left, the price goes up. If there are only a few, the price goes down. What you’re paying for is the number of harvests.
Don’t cheat one another. Show reverence for your God, because I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Keep my laws and follow my instructions, and you’ll live safely in the land.
The land will produce its crops, you’ll have enough to eat your fill, and you’ll live there safely.
You might ask, “What will we eat in year seven if we can’t plant anything or bring in a harvest?”
I’ll send my blessing on you in year six, so the land will grow enough food for three years.
You’ll plant in year eight and keep eating from what you stored up until year nine. Eat from those supplies until the new harvest comes in.
“‘Don’t sell the land away for good. The land is mine, and you live with me as foreigners and guests.
Wherever you own land, you must allow it to be bought back.
“‘If one of your people falls into poverty and sells some of their property, their closest relative can come and buy back what they sold.
If they have nobody to buy it back but they get back on their feet and come up with enough money,
they’ll work out how many years have passed since the sale, pay the buyer back for the years still left, and return to their property.
If they can’t buy it back, it stays with the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee the property goes free, and the original owner returns to it.
“‘If someone sells a home in a walled city, they have one year from the sale to buy it back. That right lasts a full year.
If the house isn’t bought back within that year, it belongs to the buyer and their descendants in perpetuity. It won’t go back in the Jubilee.
Houses in villages without walls count as open farmland. They can be bought back, and they’ll go back to the original owners in the Jubilee.
“‘The Levites can buy back homes in the cities they own at any time.
A Levite can buy back a house sold in one of their cities. It’ll be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the Levites’ cities are their property among the Israelites.
The pasturelands around their cities can’t be sold. Those lands belong to them forever.
“‘If one of your people falls into poverty and can’t keep themselves afloat, help them out so they can live with you like a foreigner or a temporary resident.
Don’t charge them interest or make a profit off them. Show reverence for your God so your neighbor can stay and live among you.
Don’t lend them money at interest or sell them food for a profit.
I’m Yahweh your God. I brought you out of Egypt to give you Canaan and to be your God.
“‘If one of your people falls into poverty and sells themselves to you, don’t make them work as a slave.
They’ll stay with you as a hired worker and temporary resident and work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
Then they’ll leave with their children, return to their family, and go back to their family’s land.
They’re my servants. I brought them out of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves.
Don’t treat them harshly. Show reverence for your God.
“‘As for male and female slaves, you may buy them from the nations around you.
You may also buy from the children of foreigners living with you and from their families who have had children in your land. They’ll become your property.
You may leave them to your children as an inheritance and hold them as slaves for life. But when it comes to your fellow Israelites, don’t rule harshly over one another.
“‘If a foreigner living among you gets rich while one of your own people falls into poverty and sells themselves to that foreigner or to someone in the foreigner’s family,
they can still be bought back after the sale. One of their brothers can buy them back,
or their uncle, cousin, or any close relative in their family. If they come into enough money, they can buy their own freedom.
They’ll work out the price with the person who bought them. Count the years from the sale to the Jubilee and price those years at the rate of a hired worker.
If lots of years are left, they’ll pay back the share of the original price that covers those years to buy their freedom.
If only a few years are left until the Jubilee, they’ll work out the amount with the buyer and pay the share for the years left to serve.
Treat them like a worker hired year by year. Don’t let the buyer rule over them harshly while you stand by.
If they aren’t bought back in one of these ways, they and their children will go free in the Year of Jubilee.
The Israelites are my servants. I brought them out of Egypt. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Don’t make idols for yourselves, set up a carved image or a pillar, or put a carved stone in your land to bow down to it. I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Keep my Sabbaths and treat my sanctuary with reverence. I’m Yahweh.
“‘If you live by my laws, remember my commands, and actually do what they say,
I’ll send rain when it’s due. The land will grow crops, and the trees in the fields will bear fruit.
You’ll still be threshing grain when it’s time to pick grapes, and you’ll still be picking grapes when it’s time to plant. You’ll eat your fill of bread and live safely in your land.
“‘I’ll give your land peace. You’ll lie down with nobody to scare you. I’ll clear dangerous animals out of the land, and the sword won’t sweep through it.
You’ll chase your enemies, and they’ll fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
“‘I’ll look on you with favor, make you fruitful, grow your numbers, and establish my covenant with you.
You’ll still be eating food you stored long ago when you have to clear it out to make room for the new harvest.
I’ll set up my tent among you, and I won’t turn away from you in disgust.
I’ll walk among you. I’ll be your God, and you’ll be my people.
I’m Yahweh your God. I brought you out of Egypt so you wouldn’t be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and got you walking with your heads up.
“‘But if you won’t listen to me or follow all these commands,
if you reject my laws and despise my instructions so much that you refuse to do what I commanded and break my covenant,

here’s what I’ll do to you: I’ll bring terror, wasting disease, and fever that dims your eyes and drains the life out of you. You’ll plant your seed for nothing because your enemies will eat what grows.
I’ll turn against you, and your enemies will beat you. The people who hate you will rule over you. You’ll run even when nobody is chasing you.
“‘If you still won’t listen after all that, I’ll punish you seven times more for your sins.
I’ll break the power you’re so proud of. I’ll make the sky above you like iron and the soil under you like bronze.
You’ll wear yourselves out for nothing. Your land won’t grow crops, and its trees won’t bear fruit.
“‘If you keep going against me and won’t listen, I’ll bring seven times more trouble on you for your sins.
I’ll send wild animals among you. They’ll take your children, destroy your livestock, and leave so few of you that your roads will be empty.
“‘If all this still doesn’t turn you back to me and you keep going against me,
I’ll go against you too. I myself will strike you seven times for your sins.
I’ll bring the sword against you to avenge the covenant. You’ll crowd into your cities, and I’ll send disease among you. You’ll be handed over to the enemy.
When I cut off your bread supply, ten women will bake all your bread in one oven and hand it back by weight. You’ll eat and still be hungry.
“‘If even then you won’t listen and keep going against me,
I’ll go against you in anger and punish you seven times for your sins.
You’ll eat the flesh of your sons and daughters.
I’ll tear down your worship sites on the heights and cut down your incense altars. I’ll throw your dead bodies on the lifeless bodies of your idols, and I’ll despise you.
I’ll leave your cities in ruins and your sanctuaries deserted. I won’t take any pleasure in the smell of your offerings.
I’ll devastate the land. Even your enemies who settle there will be stunned by it.
I’ll scatter you among the nations and draw my sword to go after you. Your land will be deserted, and your cities will be in ruins.
Then the land will finally get its Sabbaths. While it lies deserted and you live in your enemies’ land, it’ll rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
For as long as it lies deserted, it’ll get the rest it missed on your Sabbaths while you lived on it.

“‘I’ll make those of you who survive lose heart in your enemies’ lands. Even the sound of a leaf blowing past will send them running like they’re fleeing a sword. They’ll fall with nobody after them. 🍂
They’ll trip over one another like people trying to escape a sword, even with nobody after them. You won’t have the strength to stand up to your enemies.
You’ll die among the nations. Your enemies’ land will swallow you up.
Those of you who are left will waste away in your enemies’ lands because of what you did wrong. You’ll also waste away because of the wrongs your ancestors did.
“‘But if they admit what they and their ancestors did wrong, how they were unfaithful to me, and admit that because they went against me
I went against them and brought them into their enemies’ land, if their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they accept the punishment for what they did,
then I’ll remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham. I’ll remember the land too.

They’ll leave the land behind, and it’ll enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies deserted without them. They’ll accept the punishment for what they did, because they rejected my instructions and despised my laws.
Even after all that, when they’re in their enemies’ land, I won’t reject them or despise them so completely that I destroy them and break my covenant with them. I’m Yahweh their God.
For their sake I’ll remember the covenant with their ancestors, the ones I brought out of Egypt in front of the nations so I could be their God. I’m Yahweh.’”
These are the laws, instructions, and teachings Yahweh established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘If someone makes a vow setting a person apart for Yahweh, here’s how to work out the value:
For a male from twenty to sixty years old, set the value at fifty silver shekels, using the sanctuary shekel.
For a female in that age group, set it at thirty shekels.
From five to twenty years old, set it at twenty shekels for a male and ten for a female.
From one month to five years old, set it at five silver shekels for a male and three for a female.
From sixty years old and up, set it at fifteen shekels for a male and ten for a female.
If the person who made the vow can’t afford that amount, bring them before the priest. The priest will set a value based on what they can afford.
“‘If the vow is for an animal of a kind people can offer to Yahweh, any such animal given to Yahweh becomes holy.
Don’t swap it out, whether you’d be trading a good one for a bad one or a bad one for a good one. If you make a swap anyway, both animals become holy.
If it’s an unclean animal, the kind nobody offers to Yahweh, bring it before the priest.
The priest will assess its condition, good or bad. Whatever value he sets is what stands.
If you want to buy the animal back, add a fifth to that value.
“‘When someone dedicates their house to Yahweh as holy, the priest will assess its condition, good or bad. The value the priest sets is final.
If the person who dedicated it wants the house back, they’ll pay the assessed value plus a fifth. Then the house is theirs.
“‘When someone dedicates part of their own field to Yahweh, base its value on how much seed it takes to plant it. Set the value at fifty silver shekels for land that takes a homer of barley seed.
If they dedicate the field in the Year of Jubilee, the full assessed value stands.
If they dedicate the field after the Jubilee, the priest will work out its value by how many years remain until the next Jubilee and reduce the assessed value accordingly.
If the person who dedicated the field wants it back, they’ll pay the assessed value plus a fifth, and it’ll stay theirs.
If they don’t buy it back or they sell it to someone else, the field can no longer be bought back.
When the field is released at the Jubilee, it’ll be holy to Yahweh as land permanently devoted to him. It’ll belong to the priests.
“‘If someone dedicates a field to Yahweh that they bought and that isn’t part of their own family land,
the priest will calculate its value up to the Year of Jubilee. The person will pay that amount the same day as something set apart for Yahweh.
In the Year of Jubilee, the field will go back to the person who sold it, the one whose family land it is.
Use the sanctuary shekel for every valuation. A shekel is twenty gerahs.
“‘Nobody may dedicate a firstborn animal, whether it’s a firstborn ox or sheep. The firstborn already belongs to Yahweh.
If it’s an unclean animal, the owner may buy it back at the assessed value plus a fifth. If it isn’t bought back, sell it for the assessed value.

“‘Anything someone permanently devotes to Yahweh from what they own, whether a person, an animal, or part of their land, can’t be sold or bought back. Everything permanently devoted is most holy to Yahweh.
“‘A person devoted to destruction can’t be ransomed. That person must be put to death.
“‘A tenth of all the land produces, whether crops from seed or fruit from trees, belongs to Yahweh. It’s holy to him.
If you want to buy back any of your tenth, pay an extra fifth.
As the cattle, sheep, or goats pass under the counting rod, every tenth animal is holy to Yahweh.
Don’t check whether that animal is good or bad, and don’t swap it out. If you do make a swap, both animals become holy. Neither may be bought back.’”
These are the commands Yahweh gave Moses on Mount Sinai for the Israelites.
